title: The `static` keyword: when something belongs to the class, not the object

videos.script: Every field so far has had one copy per object. Two members, two names, two counts of loans. This lesson is about the field that has one copy, full stop. {{fields}} Mark a field static and it belongs to the class. Every member sees the same one. That is exactly right for a count of how many members exist. {{methods}} A static method belongs to the class too. You call it on the class's name, with no object at all. Which is why main is static: when the JVM starts, there is no object yet to call it on. {{pitfalls}} Then the traps. A static field meant to be shared, and one shared by mistake. And a constant the compiler copies into every class that uses it, so changing it in one place changes nothing until the others are compiled again. By the end you can tell what belongs to the class and what belongs to each object.
